subject: ela
intro: Read each informational passage carefully. Then choose the answer that is best supported by the exact words of the text. Cite what the text states or what you can reasonably infer from it, not what you already knew.

items.prompt:
Passage: The Saturn V rocket carried astronauts to the Moon. Standing 363 feet tall, it remains the most powerful rocket ever flown. Its first stage burned fuel at a rate of nearly 15 tons per second.

Which sentence from the passage directly states how tall the Saturn V rocket was?
A) The Saturn V rocket carried astronauts to the Moon.
B) Standing 363 feet tall, it remains the most powerful rocket ever flown.
C) Its first stage burned fuel at a rate of nearly 15 tons per second.
D) The rocket was taller than any building in its launch area.
items.answer: B) Standing 363 feet tall, it remains the most powerful rocket ever flown.

steps: The question asks for the sentence that directly states the rocket's height.
B) is correct because it gives the height explicitly: 'Standing 363 feet tall.'
A) names what the rocket did but says nothing about its height.
C) gives the fuel rate, not the height.
D) is not in the passage at all; it relies on an outside assumption the text never states.
solution.answer: B) Standing 363 feet tall, it remains the most powerful rocket ever flown.

items.prompt:
Passage: The Komodo dragon is the largest lizard on Earth. A full-grown adult can reach 10 feet in length and weigh about 150 pounds. It hunts deer, pigs, and even water buffalo.

Which quotation from the passage directly states how much a full-grown Komodo dragon can weigh?
A) The Komodo dragon is the largest lizard on Earth.
B) It hunts deer, pigs, and even water buffalo.
C) A full-grown adult can reach 10 feet in length and weigh about 150 pounds.
D) The dragon is heavier than most other reptiles.
items.answer: C) A full-grown adult can reach 10 feet in length and weigh about 150 pounds.

steps: The question asks for the sentence that explicitly states the dragon's weight.
C) is correct because it states the weight directly: 'weigh about 150 pounds.'
A) describes its size in general terms but gives no weight.
B) describes what it eats, not its weight.
D) is a reader conclusion that the passage never states word for word, so it is not an explicit quotation.
solution.answer: C) A full-grown adult can reach 10 feet in length and weigh about 150 pounds.

items.prompt:
Passage: The Great Wall of China was built over many centuries. Different rulers added sections to keep out invaders from the north. Together, all its branches stretch more than 13,000 miles.

Which sentence directly states why different rulers added sections to the wall?
A) The Great Wall of China was built over many centuries.
B) Different rulers added sections to keep out invaders from the north.
C) Together, all its branches stretch more than 13,000 miles.
D) The wall took thousands of workers to complete.
items.answer: B) Different rulers added sections to keep out invaders from the north.

steps: The question asks for the sentence that explicitly states the reason rulers added sections.
B) is correct because it states the purpose directly: 'to keep out invaders from the north.'
A) says the wall was built over many centuries, which is the time span of construction, not the reason for adding sections.
C) gives the total length, not the reason.
D) is not in the passage; it adds outside information the text never states.
solution.answer: B) Different rulers added sections to keep out invaders from the north.

items.prompt:
Passage: Sea otters spend most of their lives in cold ocean water. Unlike seals and whales, they have no blubber to keep warm. Instead, they have the thickest fur of any animal, with up to a million hairs packed into a single square inch. They must eat about a quarter of their body weight in food every day just to keep their bodies warm. When their fur gets dirty, they spend hours grooming it to keep it working.

Which detail best supports the idea that sea otters depend on their fur, not blubber, to survive the cold?
A) Sea otters spend most of their lives in cold ocean water.
B) Unlike seals and whales, they have no blubber to keep warm.
C) They must eat about a quarter of their body weight in food every day.
D) When their fur gets dirty, they spend hours grooming it.
items.answer: B) Unlike seals and whales, they have no blubber to keep warm.

steps: The inference is that otters rely on fur instead of blubber to stay warm.
B) is the best support because it directly contrasts otters with blubber-having animals and says they have none, which is exactly why they must rely on fur.
A) sets the scene but does not address fur versus blubber.
C) is a true detail about their diet, but eating to make heat is a different point from relying on fur instead of blubber.
D) shows they care for the fur, but it is weaker support for the specific claim that fur replaces blubber.
solution.answer: B) Unlike seals and whales, they have no blubber to keep warm.

items.prompt:
Passage: For thousands of years, sailors had no reliable way to know their exact location at sea. They could measure how far north or south they were, but not how far east or west. Many ships were wrecked because their crews guessed wrong. In 1714, the British government offered a large cash prize to anyone who could solve the problem. A clockmaker named John Harrison spent decades building a clock accurate enough to do it. His invention saved countless lives.

Which statement is an inference rather than something the passage states directly?
A) Sailors could measure how far north or south they were, but not how far east or west.
B) In 1714, the British government offered a large cash prize.
C) Finding location at sea was an important and dangerous problem worth solving.
D) A clockmaker named John Harrison built a clock to solve the problem.
items.answer: C) Finding location at sea was an important and dangerous problem worth solving.

steps: An inference is a reasonable conclusion the reader draws; an explicit statement is written word for word in the text.
C) is correct because the passage never says the problem was 'important and dangerous worth solving.' The reader infers this from facts like wrecked ships and a large prize.
A) is stated directly in the second sentence.
B) is stated directly: the government offered a prize in 1714.
D) is stated directly: Harrison built a clock to solve the problem.
solution.answer: C) Finding location at sea was an important and dangerous problem worth solving.

items.prompt:
Passage: Coral reefs cover less than one percent of the ocean floor. Yet they are home to about a quarter of all ocean species. Fish use the reefs for shelter, food, and places to lay eggs. Many medicines have been developed from creatures that live only on reefs. Coastlines near reefs are also protected, because the reefs break the force of large waves before they reach the shore.

Which detail best supports the idea that coral reefs are valuable to humans?
A) Coral reefs cover less than one percent of the ocean floor.
B) Yet they are home to about a quarter of all ocean species.
C) Many medicines have been developed from creatures that live only on reefs.
D) Fish use the reefs for shelter, food, and places to lay eggs.
items.answer: C) Many medicines have been developed from creatures that live only on reefs.

steps: The claim is specifically about value to humans.
C) is the best support because medicines for people come directly from reef creatures, a clear human benefit.
A) is a striking opening fact about size, but it does not show value to humans.
B) shows value to ocean species, not specifically to humans.
D) describes how fish use reefs, which is a benefit to fish rather than to humans.
solution.answer: C) Many medicines have been developed from creatures that live only on reefs.

items.prompt:
Passage: Honeybees communicate with one another in a surprising way. When a scout bee finds a good source of flowers, she returns to the hive and performs a 'waggle dance.' The direction she moves points the other bees toward the flowers. The length of her waggle tells them how far away the food is. Other bees crowd around to feel and follow the dance. Within minutes, dozens of bees fly off in the correct direction. Scientists once thought only humans could share such detailed directions. The dance shows that a tiny insect can pass along precise information using movement alone.

A reader claims: 'The waggle dance lets bees share not just that food exists, but exactly where to find it.' Which quotation gives the strongest support for this claim?
A) Other bees crowd around to feel and follow the dance.
B) The direction she moves points the other bees toward the flowers, and the length of her waggle tells them how far away the food is.
C) Scientists once thought only humans could share such detailed directions.
D) When a scout bee finds a good source of flowers, she returns to the hive.
items.answer: B) The direction she moves points the other bees toward the flowers, and the length of her waggle tells them how far away the food is.

steps: The claim has two parts: bees share where the food is, both direction and distance.
B) is the strongest evidence because it states both the direction (which way) and the distance (how far), which is exactly the precise location the claim describes.
A) shows bees pay attention to the dance, but it does not say location information is shared.
C) is a true detail about scientists' old beliefs, but it does not show what information the dance carries.
D) only tells when the dance begins, not that it communicates a precise location.
solution.answer: B) The direction she moves points the other bees toward the flowers, and the length of her waggle tells them how far away the food is.

items.prompt:
Passage: In the 1800s, most city streets were lit by gas lamps. A lamplighter walked the streets each evening to light every lamp by hand, then returned at dawn to put them out. The flames were dim and could be blown out by wind or rain. In 1879, Thomas Edison demonstrated a practical electric light bulb. Cities began stringing wires and replacing gas lamps with electric ones. Electric lights were brighter, steadier, and did not need a person to light them one by one. By 1900, many large cities glowed with electric light through the night, and the job of the lamplighter slowly disappeared.

Which quotation best supports the inference that electric lighting was more practical than gas lighting?
A) A lamplighter walked the streets each evening to light every lamp by hand.
B) In 1879, Thomas Edison demonstrated a practical electric light bulb.
C) Electric lights were brighter, steadier, and did not need a person to light them one by one.
D) By 1900, many large cities glowed with electric light through the night.
items.answer: C) Electric lights were brighter, steadier, and did not need a person to light them one by one.

steps: The inference is that electric lighting was more practical than gas lighting, so the best evidence must compare the two.
C) is the strongest support because it directly contrasts electric lights with the gas system, showing they were brighter, steadier, and needed no lamplighter, which is what 'more practical' means.
A) describes the gas system alone and does not compare it to electric light.
B) tells when the bulb appeared but does not explain why it was more practical.
D) shows electric light spread widely, an effect of being practical rather than the reason it was more practical.
solution.answer: C) Electric lights were brighter, steadier, and did not need a person to light them one by one.
